Irene — technical breakdown below. TL;DR: feasible with a scoped configuration and small infra changes.

Current behavior:
- Standard backups/snapshots: automated daily snapshots, retained 30 days, global prune job removes older snapshots.
- Application diagnostic/transient logs: normally TTLed to 30 days and included in same lifecycle for cost reasons.

Proposal to satisfy HealthSync:
1) Create an isolated S3 prefix/bucket for HealthSync tenant-logs (name: healthsync-tenant-logs) with object lifecycle rule 90-day expiration.
2) Exclude that prefix from the global snapshot/prune job. Snapshots remain 30d; logs retained 90d.
3) Implement a tag-based billing meter and a small alert to flag objects >80d for ops visibility.
4) If customer requires longer than 90d later, treat as case-by-case with cost approval.

Subprocessors:
- The only subprocessor who could see logs for longer is our archival replication partner (DataPulse). We can route HealthSync logs to a bucket in our single-tenant partition that is not forwarded to analytics pipelines; that would prevent other subprocessors from seeing them. Aaron from DataPulse would need a config flag to opt-out of replication for this prefix.

Impact/cost: estimated incremental storage ~40GB/month for HealthSync (based on their current volume), plus ~0.2 FTE operational overhead for the first 60 days of monitoring.

I've attached a quick diagram of the proposed flow. If ops/legal are aligned I can open a small infra ticket to implement the prefix and lifecycle rules.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — that approach reads fine from a legal standpoint, but a couple of notes: 

1) DPA amendment: we should add a short rider specifying the carveout: tenant-specific diagnostic logs retained for 90 days in a segregated storage bucket; Redwood will not forward those objects to analytics subprocessors unless explicitly requested. This rider can be a 1-paragraph addendum to the existing DPA and executed via DocuSign.

2) Subprocessors: we must notify any subprocessors who may have access to backups or logs. If DataPulse is configurable to opt-out from replication for the HealthSync prefix, we can avoid listing them as having access. If not, we must provide HealthSync a subprocessor notice and an opt-out clause.

3) Approval path & timing: Legal + Privacy sign-off (me + Irene) -> DocuSign -> update Subprocessor Register. I expect draft language can be provided within 24 business hours once we confirm the ops config.

I'll draft the rider and attach a suggested paragraph. Also recommend creating JIRA-INF-1123 so Compliance can track the exception and evidence of subprocessor opt-out.

Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
